intent_en: To explain the two potential outcomes of a pandemic outbreak—fast and slow spread—and how early reactions determine the shape of the infection curve over time.
previous_intent: To illustrate the two potential trajectories of a pandemic outbreak, contrasting a rapid, high-volume spread with a slower, more gradual spread to demonstrate how early reactions influence the timeline of infections.
narration_support: There are two futures for a pandemic like corona, fast and slow. Which future we will see depends on how we will react to it in the early days of the outbreak.
chart_support: Area chart plotting Infections against Time, showing a high, narrow 'Fast Spread' curve and a lower, wider 'Slow Spread' curve originating from an 'Outbreak'.
evidence_note: The narration explicitly defines two futures (fast/slow) and the role of early reaction, while the chart visualizes these exact two scenarios as infection curves over time.
